clue.text: Man eats first of ripe bananas as side dish

indicators.note: one piece eating another means it takes the other inside itself

parts.note: a man in chess is a piece, and the humblest is a pawn

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: bananas and crackers are both slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into ripe bananas as an accompaniment to a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece here, not a person. A side dish of PRAWN CRACKERS is common with Chinese takeaway food.
explanation.definitionFit: These puffed crisps are served alongside a main course, which makes them a side dish.

clue.text: Early starter?

parts.note: read as the thing life is said to have started from in the earliest days of the Earth, not a first course at a meal

explanation.surface: Something served first at an early meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The broth of chemicals in which life supposedly began is the very earliest starter of all.

clue.text: A voyage northward, one's assumed

indicators.note: in a down clue, going northward means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to sail is to voyage

explanation.surface: Someone takes for granted a trip heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is a false name, one that a person has assumed.

clue.text: Not entirely pleasant extremists banished from country, north Central American

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word, its extremes, are sent away

parts.note: Paraguay is a country in South America

explanation.surface: Radicals who are none too nice have been exiled from a country in the north of Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts NICE to NIC; 'extremists banished from' strips P and Y from PARAGUAY, leaving ARAGUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nicaragua is a Central American by nationality.

clue.text: Chorus one whistles, then drops

parts.note: a referee is the official who blows the whistle
rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: A football official blows the whistle and then collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the repeated chorus of a song.

clue.text: Company record, a bit of a bloomer

parts.note: a roll is an official list or record, as in an electoral roll

explanation.surface: A firm's documents contain a small mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The corolla is the ring of petals, one part of a flower.

clue.text: Each way? No, just one

parts.note: ST, for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A punter asks for an each-way bet and is told only one option is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: An each-way bet covers both a win and a place; here it splits into abbreviations. The definition is one single compass point, as opposed to the two ways of an each-way bet.
explanation.definitionFit: The east is one compass direction, a single way out of the four.

clue.text: Out-of-this-world experience sealed by lover, having popped speed

indicators.note: the first piece has another popped into it, put inside

parts.note: SWALK, Sealed With A Loving Kiss, is written on the backs of love letters in Britain
pace means speed

explanation.surface: A lover's letter tells of a mind-blowing trip taken on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: SWALK is an old British envelope acronym for 'Sealed With A Loving Kiss'. 'Popped speed' suggests taking an amphetamine.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in space, outside a craft, is literally an experience beyond this world.

clue.text: Dubious telly hero, or dim drag act

indicators.note: something dubious is not quite right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A questionable television hero, or else a dull cross-dressing routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Riley was a British music-hall and film character, an Irish washerwoman played by the comedian Arthur Lucan in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: This character was a male comedian dressed as an old woman, a classic drag act.

clue.text: I suffer back condition, primarily through the hip-bone

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, relating to the hip-bone

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to suffer

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone describes the painful back trouble that runs through their hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac means relating to the ilium, the large upper bone of the pelvis, so 'through the hip-bone' fits loosely.

clue.text: Prevent old place entering collapse

indicators.note: entering means these pieces go inside the other word

parts.note: to fall is to collapse
to place something is to rest it, set it down

explanation.surface: Stopping an ancient building from falling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' is a verb here, as in putting something down, so it gives REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall something is to act early so that it cannot happen, so to prevent it.

clue.text: Babe cavorting with lovers on offer at peepshow?

indicators.note: cavorting means jumping about, so the letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: A girl romps with her lovers in a seedy peepshow.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything at a peepshow is there to be viewed, so it is observable, with a cheeky question mark.

clue.text: A supportive smile?

parts.note: read as one word meaning both a structural support, like a timber in a roof, and a broad smile

explanation.surface: An encouraging grin.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is both a load-bearing timber and a wide happy smile, so it is a supportive grin twice over.

clue.text: Filthy crows making racket

parts.note: blue means smutty or filthy, as in a blue film
a murder of crows is the collective noun for a group of them

explanation.surface: Dirty birds are making a terrible noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Screaming BLUE MURDER is a British idiom for making a loud fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue murder means an uproar, a loud din of complaint, so a racket.

clue.text: Figure fellow holding good card's twisting

indicators.note: holding means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: twisting means these letters are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: an ace is a playing card; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A man with a fine card in his hand is cheating at a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' turns the good card round to give ECAG; 'Figure' looks like a verb but is the geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a ten-sided geometric figure.

clue.text: Arrogance — wanting raise, one's going to head

parts.note: to cock is to raise, as in cocking an eyebrow
I is the Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone vain does not want a pay rise because success has gone to their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to head' reads as the idiom for vanity, but it says one is put in front of the head. 'wanting' and 's are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockiness is swaggering overconfidence, a form of arrogance.

clue.text: Anyway, key opens in the end

indicators.note: the key opens the phrase, getting inside it

parts.note: at last means finally, in the end
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets the key to open a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: At least, used as a sentence adverb, means anyway or in any case.

clue.text: Very old main road beginning to crumble

parts.note: arch means chief or main, as in arch-enemy
AI stands for the A1, Britain's Great North Road, with the figure written as I

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An ancient highway is starting to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main road' reads as one phrase, but 'main' is a separate adjective meaning chief, and the road is Britain's A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to a much earlier period, so very old.

clue.text: Giants having joint deficit, current

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning joint, as in co-owner
a loss is a deficit
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Big companies are running a combined deficit at present.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi is the plural of colossus, a giant statue or giant figure.

clue.text: Mark wants French community killed, every other one

parts.note: EC stands for the European Community

indicators.note: every other one means alternate letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A scar shows that every second person in a French village was killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every other one' takes K, L, E from 'killed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freckle is a small brown spot, a mark on the skin.

clue.text: Cutting tree, adjust supper for logs

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Cutting tree, adjust supper for logs': FIR (tree) is clear and 'for logs' fits a firedog, but no parse of 'Cutting ... adjust supper' gives EDOG; the scan cuts this clue off and searches failed, so it looks misread.
annotationWithheld.clue: Cutting tree, adjust supper for logs

clue.text: Action in match

explanation.surface: A move made during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a legal action in court, and to suit is to match or go with.

clue.text: Left routine in real trouble, needing versatile type

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
in trouble, the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: a round is a routine, as in a daily round

explanation.surface: Someone who quit their daily routine and is now in a mess needs a person who can turn their hand to anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes ALER from the fodder; 'in' then places the left-and-routine pair after its first letter. An all-rounder in cricket both bats and bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is someone good at many things, especially a cricketer who bats and bowls, so a versatile type.

clue.text: Round mark?

parts.note: read as a mark left during a round of golf, not a circular mark

explanation.surface: A circular stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A divot is the chunk of turf gouged out by a golf club, a mark made during a round.

clue.text: Showed contempt for argument

definitions.meaning: ... on or at someone, expressing scorn

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at the reasoning put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Spat is the past tense of spit, an act of contempt, and also a small quarrel.

clue.text: Given no sex, prude runs away, sadly fully clothed?

indicators.note: sadly signals that the remaining letters are rearranged
runs away means that letter is removed

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A puritan, denied sex, sadly flees still wearing all their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' takes R out of NOSEXPRUDE, and 'sadly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fully clothed has nothing on show, so they are not exposed.

clue.text: Beast died — its nature?

parts.note: wickedness is the nature of the beast in question

explanation.surface: An animal has died, perhaps true to its character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its nature' refers back to the beast: the Devil's nature is evil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beast is a name for Satan in the Book of Revelation.

clue.text: Might supermodel be rich?

parts.note: read literally as a beautiful model who is posing, attractive while sitting, rather than asking about wealth

explanation.surface: Asking whether a top model is wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting pretty means being comfortably well off, and a posing supermodel is literally pretty while sitting.
